image.alt: A Syngonium Panda Galaxy with green arrowhead leaves speckled in cream and white, in a white pot

light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but the speckles fade

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep out of direct sun

home_use.note: Best near an east-facing window, or a few feet back from a bright one

snap: A climbing and trailing arrowhead vine with green leaves sprinkled with cream and white speckles, like stars. Every leaf comes out a little different. It grows well in a hanging basket or up a pole, and is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The species grows wild in the humid forests of Central and South America, where it scrambles over the forest floor and climbs trees. The Panda Galaxy is a cultivated, speckled form of it. It is an evergreen vine that trails from a basket or climbs to about 1.5 m with support.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light, and water when the top 2–3 cm of soil is dry. In low light the speckles fade towards plain green, and direct sun scorches the pale spots. Keep it warm, ideally 18–27°C and never below 15°C, and never let the pot sit in water, since wet roots rot easily.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The variegation is a scatter of cream and white spots, from lightly peppered to boldly marbled, and each new leaf has its own pattern. Pinch the tips to keep it full and bushy. If a shoot turns plain green, cut it back to a speckled node. A moss pole makes the leaves larger and more lobed.
